answer: A reputation ledger grows like a vine: each agent earns trust only through verified work over time, so a fake identity starts bare and cannot buy history. High-value trades require a stake of the agent's own earned credits, locked like a pearl inside the ledger until the deal settles, so a sybil that defects forfeits its stake. Newcomers stay in a marble-walled sandbox, trading only small amounts until peers attest their work, making mass fake identities expensive and slow.
